get.description: Report that the process is up. Reads no configuration and no database.

Every `resume` row, newest first, and `[]` when none was ever uploaded.

No filter and no paging: one person's resumes are few, and every upload is
history worth showing -- the active one first among them, since it is the
newest until an older one is activated again. The order and the reading of
the rows are `app.services.resume.resume_rows`'s.

post.description: Accept one file, extract its text -- or read a scan -- and store it as the active resume.

413.description: The upload is larger than the configured limit, in bytes or in page images

415.description: The declared type, or the bytes, are not a readable resume

422.description: The upload is corrupt, carries no text, or is not a named file part

502.description: The scan could not be read: the model call timed out, failed, or answered something unusable

503.description: The model key is not configured, so a scan cannot be read

patch.summary: Make one stored resume the active one
patch.description:
Make that resume the active one, and answer with it as the list renders it.

The id is a path parameter and an `int`: a value that is not one never
reaches this function and is refused by the path's own validation as `422`.
A body that says anything but "active" is refused by `ResumeActivation` the
same way, before any write. An id that finds no row is a `404` and writes
nothing. The row that was active goes inactive in the same transaction, so
one row is active afterwards and it is the one the path names; sending the
request again for the row that is already active is the same answer twice.

422.description: The body, or the path, is not something this route can use

delete.summary: Delete one stored resume and its file
delete.description:
Delete exactly that resume -- its row and the file it names -- and answer `204`.

The id is a path parameter and an `int`, refused by the path's own validation
as `422` when it is not one, and an id that finds no row is a `404` that
writes nothing. Deleting the active resume is allowed: it leaves no active
row, which is a state the app already handles. Nothing about the resume is
answered: `204` carries no body, so no part of the row -- the text above all
-- can ride along on it.

422.description: The body, or the path, is not something this route can use

get.summary: Download the stored file of one resume
get.description:
Answer with the file that resume's row names, as an attachment under the row's own type.

The id is a path parameter and an `int`, refused by the path's own validation
as `422` when it is not one, and an id that finds no row is a `404` naming it.
A row whose stored path is not a file inside the app's uploads directory -- a
path no writer here produces -- is refused before anything is opened, by the
delete's own containment rule, `app.services.resume.stored_file`; a file that
was stored and has since gone is a `404` as well, never the `500` a missing
file would otherwise be, and its detail says the stored file is missing.

The bytes belong to the response and never to this function: `FileResponse`
streams them from the path, so no line here holds them or names them, and the
log line names the resume's id and the file's size -- all a download is to
this app. The media type and the filename are the row's own, and the answer's
`content-type` is that value exactly rather than one the framework appends a
charset to, because the row's media type is the one #3 validated on the way
in.

200.description: The stored file, byte for byte, as an attachment

404.description: No resume has that id, or the file its stored path names is not in the uploads directory

422.description: The path value is not a resume id

post.summary: Parse the active resume into its name and skills
post.description:
Parse the active resume once, store its fields on its row, and answer them.

No path parameter and no request body: the resume this parses is the active
one, which is the row every other route in this family already names. A row
that already holds its fields is answered from the stored JSON without a
request, because a parse is a slow, paid call and the stored text never
changes after the upload; a NULL column is the one thing that makes a call,
and it is the row's own column, so a resume activated again later parses on
its own first call.

The two JSON directions are this module's: `json.dumps` of the object the
parser answered, and the same object read back. The failures are the
parser's own types, answered by name: the scorer's configuration error is a
`503` -- it means no key is set, which is a deployment's problem and not the
request's -- and a parse that produced no fields is a `502`, the model
upstream having failed. The log line names the resume's id and the shape of
what was stored, never a value: the fields are user data, like the text.

404.description: No resume is active, so there is nothing to parse

502.description: The model call timed out, failed, or answered something unusable

503.description: The model key is not configured, so the model cannot be asked

get.description:
Every company on the watchlist, in ascending id order, active or not.

No filter and no paging: one user's watchlist is short, and an inactive
company is still a company to show. Each row carries the source it names.

post.description:
Add one company, once the board its `source` names has answered for its slug.

The board is asked before anything is written, and every `POST` asks it once:
a body that cannot be used never reaches this function, and a slug that is
already watched is refused only after the source has spoken for it.

404.description: No board goes by that slug, or no company has that id

409.description: That slug is already watched on that source

422.description: The body, or the path, is not something this route can use

502.description: The board could not be read: it is down, slow or malformed

patch.summary: Rename a watched company, or take it out of the poll
patch.description:
Write the fields the body names on that company, and answer as `GET /watchlist` renders it.

The id is a path parameter and an `int`: a value that is not one never reaches
this function and is refused by the path's own validation as `422`, and an id
that finds no row is a `404` that writes nothing. A body naming `source` is
refused first and in full: `SOURCE_IS_FIXED` says what is wrong and what to do
instead, and neither the row nor any other table is touched, whether or not the
body also names a `slug`.

A `slug` points the company at a corrected board. The candidate goes through
the model's normaliser, and a spelling equal to the row's own is no move at
all: no board is asked, nothing is closed and the answer is the ordinary
write. A move is probed through the row's own stored `source` -- `404` when no
board goes by that name, `502` when it cannot be read -- and a pair another
company holds on that source is the `409` the unique key raises under the
flush. Every refusal precedes the close, so a refused request writes no field
and closes nothing. The move clears the validator the old board left and closes
every open posting of that company exactly once, in the same transaction as
the slug, so nothing is left open against a board this app no longer watches.

`is_active: false` takes the company out of the tick's walk and is not a
deletion: the row, its postings and their matches stay untouched, and
`GET /watchlist` keeps listing the company as inactive. `is_active` gates
nothing here, so a slug change on a deactivated company is an ordinary write.
Sending the same body again is the same answer twice, and no request here
creates a row.

404.description: No board goes by that slug, or no company has that id

409.description: That slug is already watched on that source

422.description: The body, or the path, is not something this route can use

502.description: The board could not be read: it is down, slow or malformed

delete.description:
Delete exactly that company, and answer `204` with no body when it went.

The id is a path parameter and an `int`: a value that is not one never
reaches this function and is refused by the path's own validation as `422`.
An id that finds no row is a `404` and deletes nothing.

404.description: No board goes by that slug, or no company has that id

422.description: The body, or the path, is not something this route can use

post.description:
Start one run, and answer `202` with the row this request wrote.

The shared sequence `_start_run`, with the walk-and-digest `get_pipeline()` as
the work: the caller is checked, the guard is claimed, the row is written, the
work is handed over, and the `202` carries that `running` row.

202.description: A run started: the run row this request wrote

401.description: The request is not admitted: it carried neither the shared internal header nor an Origin naming this instance's own host

409.description: A run is already in progress in this process

500.description: The run could not be recorded, or its work could not be started

post.description:
Start one re-match, and answer `202` with the row this request wrote.

The tick's own machinery, one door over: `_start_run` checks the caller through
the same shared header, claims the same in-process guard against two runs at
once, writes the same `_claim_run()` row, hands the work over through the same
`get_run_starter()` seam and records how it ended through the same `_run`. Only
the work differs -- the `get_rematch()` provider's
`pipeline.rematch_stored_postings` in place of the `get_pipeline()` provider's
walk and digest -- so the answer is a `running` `RunSummary` a client reads
through `GET /runs/{id}`, exactly as a tick's is.

202.description: A re-match started: the run row this request wrote

401.description: The request is not admitted: it carried neither the shared internal header nor an Origin naming this instance's own host

409.description: A run is already in progress in this process

500.description: The run could not be recorded, or its work could not be started

get.description:
The newest `limit` runs, newest first, and `[]` when the repository holds none.

One statement, ordered `started_at` descending with the id descending under it,
so two runs that started in the same instant -- which `started_at`'s default
makes possible -- still have one order and the newest N is never an arbitrary N.
`limit` defaults to `RUNS_DEFAULT_LIMIT` and is bounded by `RUNS_MAX_LIMIT`; `0`,
a negative value or one above the bound is refused as `422` before this function
runs. The body is the same `RunSummary` `GET /runs/{id}` answers, rendered by the
same `run_summary`, so the two routes cannot drift apart.

The run with that id, in whichever status it is in, exactly as the row holds it.

The id is a path parameter and an `int`: a value that is not one never
reaches this function and is refused by the path's own validation as `422`.
An id that finds no row is a `404` and invents nothing.

422.description: The path value is not a run id

get.description:
Every `match` row the query leaves, newest first, and `[]` when it leaves none.

No parameter means no filter, which is every row and what this route has
always answered; each parameter narrows that answer and none of them hides a
row on its own. `min_score` is a floor on the row's own score -- `0` includes
the prefiltered and the not-scored rows, because which of those to show is
#12's decision and not this read's -- `state` is one value of the column's
vocabulary, `company_id` is the company the posting belongs to (an id no row
names matches nothing and answers `[]`, not a `404`), and `limit` is the
newest N, at most `MATCHES_MAX_LIMIT`. Values outside a parameter's own range
or vocabulary are refused as `422` before this function runs and write
nothing.

The answer is one statement: the filters are `.where(...)` clauses on the read
that was already there, so they compose with AND and none of them is applied
after the rows have been read. The company filter is the posting's own column,
which is what the join is for: a match has exactly one posting (`match`'s
foreign key is `NOT NULL`), so the join drops no row. The order is `created_at`
descending with the id descending under it, so two rows written in the same
instant -- which `created_at`'s default makes possible -- still have one order,
newest row first; `limit` is applied after that ordering, so it is the newest
N and never an arbitrary N.

patch.summary: Record the owner's verdict on one match
patch.description:
Write the owner's `saved` or `dismissed` verdict on that match, and answer with it.

The id is a path parameter and an `int`: a value that is not one never
reaches this function and is refused by the path's own validation as `422`.
A body whose `state` is neither of the two verdicts is refused by
`MatchVerdict` the same way. An id that finds no row is a `404` and writes
nothing. What is written is `state` and nothing else, and the answer is the
row as `GET /matches` renders it, read after the write -- so the same verdict
sent twice is the same answer twice and one row the whole time.

422.description: The body, or the path, is not something this route can use

get.summary: Read one window of per-route metrics
get.description:
One object per route with a span in the last `METRICS_WINDOW`, ordered by route.

The window is `datetime.now(UTC) - METRICS_WINDOW` and a span that started
before it is not counted, so the same window read twice answers the same body
and a span that ages out of it stops being counted. Every span of a route in
the window is one of its `count`, the ones whose status code is >= 500 are its
`errors`, and `p95_ms` is the nearest-rank 95th percentile of its durations.

The run's own span has no route and is not a route's: it is stored, and read by
`GET /telemetry/traces`, but it is not counted here. A path no route matched is
counted under `UNMATCHED_ROUTE`, so a caller walking a 404 is visible too.

schema.title: Response Read Metrics Telemetry Metrics Get

get.summary: Read the newest traces, each with its spans
get.description:
The newest traces grouped by trace id, newest first, and `[]` when there are none.

`limit` counts traces and not spans: the newest N trace ids and every span each
one holds. Absent means every stored trace, which `SPAN_RETENTION` bounds --
the prune keeps the table finite, so this read is finite too -- and a limit of
`0`, a negative one or more than `TRACES_MAX_LIMIT` is refused as `422` before
this function runs.

A trace is as new as its latest span, and its spans are ordered by the instant
they started: a run's span starts after the request's own, so the two read in
the order the journey happened. Two traces whose latest spans share an instant
-- and two spans of one trace that do -- are ordered by id under it, so one
window reads the same body twice.

schema.title: Response Read Traces Telemetry Traces Get

422.description: The limit is not a whole number of traces this read answers

file.title: File
file.description: A PDF, a DOCX, a PNG, a JPEG, a TIFF, a HEIC, a WebP or a UTF-8 text file

CompanyCreate.title: CompanyCreate
CompanyCreate.description:
Body of an addition: the name to show, the board slug to poll, and its source.

`name` and `slug` are required strings, and a string that carries nothing but
whitespace is refused as well: the name labels a row a person reads, and the
slug is what the source is asked about. `name` is refused when it is longer
than the 255 characters `company.name` holds or carries a control character
(a NUL included) -- the column's own refusals, answered here as the `422`
this route owes instead of the `500` PostgreSQL's driver answers. `source` is
optional and means Greenhouse when it is absent, so a client that sends
`{name, slug}` keeps working; a value outside the two known names -- a case
variant included -- is a `422` from this model, before any request is made.
The values are left exactly as they were sent; normalising the slug is
`app.models.Company`'s.

CompanyUpdate.title: CompanyUpdate
CompanyUpdate.description:
Body of an edit: the label to show, the poll state, the board slug, or a combination.

Every field is optional and at least one of them has to be supplied: `{}`
is a request that says nothing, and answering it `200` would report a write
that did not happen. `name` is a label stored exactly as it arrived, refused
when it is blank (`CompanyCreate._not_blank`'s rule), carries a control
character, or is longer than the 255 characters `company.name` holds -- the
last two are the column's own refusals, and answering them here makes them
the `422` this route owes instead of the `500` PostgreSQL's driver answers.
No normaliser runs on it, because the one in `app.models` touches `slug`.
`is_active` is a `Literal` of the two booleans, so `"false"` is refused
rather than read as one: whether a board is polled is a state and not a
truthy string.

`source` is declared here and `null` means "not supplied", the way `name`
does -- a body naming only `source` is a body that names a field, so the
validator below lets it through and the *route* answers the rule it breaks,
in words an `extra="forbid"` refusal cannot carry. `slug` is the board to
point the company at (#60): normalised by `app.models.Company` and probed
through the row's own source by the route. A blank one is refused here, and
the value carries no length bound, mirroring `CompanyCreate.slug`. Nothing
clears a field: `name` is a `NOT NULL` column and `is_active` is the whole of
"is it polled".

MatchSummary.title: MatchSummary
MatchSummary.description:
One `match` row as this API renders it: the row, plus the names it points at.

The same body both routes carry, so a client reads one shape for a match
wherever it meets one. Ten fields and no eleventh: `notified_at` stays on the
row, because when an alert went out is the digest's business and not the
screen's, and nothing here is computed -- `score`, `reason`, `state` and
`outcome` are the row's own, `gaps` is the list #8 stored as JSON text, and
`id` is what `PATCH /matches/{id}` takes.

MatchVerdict.title: MatchVerdict
MatchVerdict.description:
Body of a verdict: the one value this endpoint records, and no other field.

`state` is a `Literal` of the two verdicts the owner has, so anything else --
`"new"`, `""`, a number, nothing at all -- is refused by this model's own
validation as `422` and never reaches the row. Re-opening a match as `new` is
not in `_docs/plan.md`, and the column's own vocabulary is the model's
(`ck_match_state_values`) rather than this endpoint's.

ResumeActivation.title: ResumeActivation
ResumeActivation.description:
Body of an activation: the one value this endpoint accepts, and no other field.

`is_active` is a `Literal` of `True` -- the `MatchVerdict` precedent -- so
only "make this one active" is expressible and `{"is_active": false}` is
refused by this model's own validation as `422`. The model forbids extra
fields as well: deactivation is not in `_docs/plan.md`, and a body carrying
anything else is a request this route does not understand rather than a
write it performs while ignoring what it was sent.

ResumeParsed.title: ResumeParsed
ResumeParsed.description:
Body of a parse: which resume, the name it states, and the skills it claims.

The two fields are #26's own -- `name` is `None` and `skills` is `[]` for what
the resume does not state -- and they are answered here because a parse is the
one place they belong. `ResumeSummary` is deliberately not widened to carry
them: the history routes answer five public fields and no user data.

ResumeSummary.title: ResumeSummary
ResumeSummary.description:
One `resume` row as the history routes render it: five fields, and no text.

The same body `GET /resume` lists and `PATCH /resume/{id}` answers with, so a
client reads one shape for a resume wherever it meets one. `text` and
`stored_path` are deliberately not here: the text is user data and the path
is where the server put the file, and neither is the client's business.
`is_active` is the row's own column, not a property of the order: it is true
for exactly one row, the one a run would score against.

ResumeUploaded.title: ResumeUploaded
ResumeUploaded.description: Body of a successful upload: which resume is now the active one.

RouteMetric.title: RouteMetric
RouteMetric.description:
One route's window, as `GET /telemetry/metrics` answers it.

Four fields and no fifth: `count` is every span of that route in the window,
`errors` those whose status code is 500 or more, and `p95_ms` the duration
below which 95% of them fall. The route is the stored template -- `UNMATCHED_ROUTE`
for a path no route matched -- and never a path a caller chose.

RunCompanyOutcome.title: RunCompanyOutcome
RunCompanyOutcome.description:
One company's outcome in one run, as this API renders it.

One entry per company the run's walk attempted, in the order it attempted them
(#59): `outcome` is `'fetched'`, `'not_modified'` or `'failed'`, and `error` is
the failure's own message on a `'failed'` row and NULL on every other. The slug
is the company's own, read through the key the row holds, so a client reads
which board failed without a second request. A company the run's budget never
reached has no entry here: #56's `companies_not_fetched` counts those.

RunSummary.title: RunSummary
RunSummary.description:
One `run` row as this API renders it: its columns and its per-company outcomes.

The same body a `202` from `POST /internal/tick` carries. `finished_at` and
`error` are absent until the run ends, and the two counts the walk earns are
0 from the moment the row is written: what the boards returned and how many
matches `record_score` wrote (#34), never a score computed here.
`matches_emailed` is the third: how many matches this run's own digest emailed
(#36), NULL until that digest records it -- which is the honest value for a
run still in flight, a row written before the column existed, and a run whose
send failed, and a different answer from a run that really did email none.
`companies_not_fetched` is NULL for a run the board-call budget did not stop,
which includes a run still in flight, and holds the count of active companies
the walk left for a later run when it did (#56). `postings_not_rematched` is
the same shape for a re-match: NULL for every tick and every row written
before the column existed, `0` for a re-match that decided every candidate it
found, and a positive count of the passers its cap left for a later run (#64).
`company_outcomes` is one entry per company the run attempted and is empty for
a run that has not attempted one yet -- the `202`'s fresh row -- so a client
reads the same shape from both routes at every point in a run's life.
`trace_id` is the trace of the request that started this run (#102), the id the
request's own span and the run's span share; NULL means the row names no trace
-- a row written before the column existed, or a run a starter was handed
without an id -- and is never guessed at.

SpanSummary.title: SpanSummary
SpanSummary.description:
One span as the trace read renders it: the row's own facts, minus the trace id.

The id belongs to the trace this span is listed under, so it is not repeated
here, and `route`, `method` and `status_code` are `None` on a run's span.

TraceSummary.title: TraceSummary
TraceSummary.description:
One trace: the id its spans share, and those spans in the order they started.

These two key names are what #91 renders and what #92 and #93 quote when they
name a trace id, so neither may be renamed here.

WatchedCompany.title: WatchedCompany
WatchedCompany.description:
One watchlist entry as this API renders it: five fields, and no timestamp.

The same body `POST` answers with, so a client reads one shape for a company
wherever it sees one. `created_at` is stored and not exposed. `source` is the
board the row names, defaulted here so it is not a required property of the
contract: a client that already reads `{id, name, slug, is_active}` is not
broken by the extra field.
